title: Tables, columns, code and equations
p: Use a table to compare several things across the same dimensions, and columns to put independent ideas side by side. Code blocks keep scripts readable with syntax highlighting and line numbers, and LaTeX equations sit naturally alongside your writing.
Choose Table from the slash menu and select a size in the grid, up to 9 × 9. Press ⌘ ⌥ A to insert a 3 × 3 table directly. Tables pasted from Markdown, web pages or Feishu become editable tables too.
This example combines header cells, a merged row, backgrounds, alignment, tasks and lists.

Select cells: drag from one cell to another to select a rectangular range.
Select a row or column: click its gray handle. Hold Shift to extend the selection.
Insert rows or columns: hover between their handles and click the plus control.
Reorder: select a row or column, then drag it.
Resize: drag a column boundary. The block menu can distribute column widths evenly.
Delete: select a row or column and use the toolbar's delete control.

td.p: Merge a rectangular selection into one cell, or split a previously merged cell.
Use cell colors to show groups or status.
Align left, center or right; place content at the top, middle or bottom.
Apply bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, code or text colors to the selected cells.

p: Enable a header row in the table's block menu to style the first row and keep it visible while scrolling a long table. A header column styles the first column for comparison tables.
Cells can hold paragraphs, headings, lists, tasks, code and equations. Press Enter to add another paragraph within a cell.

pre.code: git switch -c feature/table git push -u origin HEAD

td.p: Code blocks make useful command references.
Mix equations with text and multiple paragraphs.

callout.p: Paste a Markdown table made with | separators to create a table. Initial column widths follow the content: short columns stay compact and longer text gets more room. You can still drag column boundaries to resize them. Markdown export writes tables in that format too.

p: Choose Columns from the slash menu, then choose one to five columns. Each column is an independent area that can contain other blocks.

column.p: Press ⌘ ⇧ N for a new note window and write down the idea.
Group related pages and pin the essentials and useful references.
Search with ⌘ J and follow backlinks to connected notes.

p: Drag the gap between columns. Widths gently snap near equal splits and simple proportions.

column.p: A calm, reliable writing tool that keeps your notes in your hands

ul.li: Hover between columns and click the plus control to add one, up to ten columns.
Remove all content from a column to remove that column. When only one remains, the layout returns to ordinary blocks.

p: Use inline code for commands, filenames and function names: brew install ripgrep or ~/.zshrc. Wrap text in backticks as you type, or select it and press ⌘ ⌃ C.

ul.li: Type three backticks at the start of a line, then Space or Enter. Add a language, as in ```python, to select it immediately.
Choose Code block from the slash menu, or press ⌘ ⌥ C.
Use the block menu to turn an existing paragraph into code.

p: Inside a code block, Tab inserts four spaces, Shift-Tab reduces indentation, and Enter starts a new line. Markdown formatting is disabled and pasted content is treated as plain text.
Hover over a code block to choose its language. The searchable picker supports more than seventy languages.

Set the language to Mermaid and Quiet.md draws the code as a diagram: flowcharts, sequence diagrams, Gantt charts and more. Hover over it and choose Hide diagram to edit the code; Show diagram brings the picture back. Markdown in Quiet.md has an example.

p: Click the caption above a code block to give it a filename or a useful description. Long lines scroll horizontally by default. Enable wrapping in the block's controls when you would rather read them without scrolling.

ul.li: The copy button copies the complete code block without its line numbers.
Use the triangle on the left to fold a long block.
The document theme controls line numbers. Craft, Feishu and Obsidian show them; Notion does not.

p: Type LaTeX between dollar signs: $a^2+b^2=c^2$ becomes a^2+b^2=c^2 when you type the closing dollar sign. Double-dollar delimiters work too.
You can also choose Equation from the slash menu. Press Esc to finish editing. Click an existing equation to edit it again; invalid input is marked without damaging the document.
The quadratic equation ax^2 + bx + c = 0 has solutions x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}. When \Delta = b^2 - 4ac < 0, it has no real solutions.
